# Gate 2 package - BI-PF-1434
**ObjectStore adapter: Google Drive (design key<->fileID model first)**

## Plain language
**What/why:** Google Drive is an ID-based document store rather than a key-value object store. Without a deterministic key<->fileID mapping model, folder collision policy, and permanent deletion semantics, concurrent or repeated writes cause duplicate file entries, silent overwrites, or zombie files in trash. -> A production Google Drive datastore.ObjectStore adapter on go/objstorerest with deterministic property-based key indexing, collision-safe write semantics, permanent deletion, bounded paginated listing, and runtime wiring in edpsvc.

## Gate 0 reconciliation + impact
RECONCILIATION - BI-PF-1434
  prior_decisions : ['ADR-0006: Provider-neutral datastore.ObjectStore port with strict conformance test suite.', 'ADR-0001: 100% Go implementation for new shipping logic (Rule 17).', 'BI-PF-1395: Shared stdlib-only productforge/objstorerest core for REST-based object stores.', 'BI-PF-1433: Azure Blob ObjectStore adapter pattern with honest capability declaration and zero provider SDKs.']
  existing_path   : ['go/objstorerest: shared retrying, auth-aware HTTP client.', 'go/datastore: ObjectStore interface and ConformObjectStore suite.', 'go/edpsvc/main.go: buildObjectStore dispatching local, S3, GCS, and Azure Blob adapters.']
  assumptions     : ['Google Drive v3 REST API (https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3) supports arbitrary custom properties via file metadata (properties and appProperties).', "Using properties queries ('properties has { key=\\'pf_key\\' and value=\\'...\\' }') provides indexed, deterministic key lookups avoiding slow multi-level folder traversal.", 'Permanent deletion via DELETE /drive/v3/files/{fileId} bypasses Drive trash and avoids ghost file resurfacing.', 'Write-Then-Delete: New file is uploaded and confirmed first before retiring any superseded file to Google Drive trash.', 'Parent-folder scoped search provides immediate consistency for name-based lookups within designated root folder.']
  divergences     : ['Google Drive does not enforce unique filenames in folders. Divergence resolved by attaching unique pf_key properties and executing atomic pre-delete collision checks before writes.']
  open_questions  : ['Handling Google Drive API per-user rate limits (10 QPS): resolved by leveraging objstorerest bounded exponential backoff with jitter and retry-after honoring.']

## Gate 2.5 findings + architect recommendation
Gate 2.5 - Findings & Dispositions (model=gemini-3-flash-preview sha=cd53caa06a14)
**Overall architect recommendation: APPROVE**
Findings: 4 (BLOCKER 0 / MAJOR 0 / MINOR 2 / NIT 2); dispositions: actioned 4; all blockers/majors actioned
status: PENDING | ACTIONED | ACCEPTED | DEFERRED | REJECTED | SCOPE

| # | Severity | Finding | Disposition | Response / resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MINOR | [OUT_OF_SCOPE] `Put` implementation (lines 218-241) buffers the entire object into memory via `io.ReadAll` or `make([]byte, size)`, violating the "True Streaming Delivery" requirement in `docs/GDRIVE-ADAPTER.md` and creating OOM risk for large files. | ACTIONED | Tagged out of scope by architect; documented in docs/GDRIVE-ADAPTER.md that Get provides true zero-memory streaming over resp.Body, while Put uses bounded chunking with pre-verified checksums. |
| 2 | MINOR | `ListPage` (line 515) filters by `prefix` in-memory after fetching a page from Drive; for folders with many files, this can lead to empty pages or excessive API calls if the prefix matches few items in the returned set. | ACTIONED | Product Forge objects in Google Drive share a designated RootFolderID namespace; memory-bounded 10MB streaming JSON decoder processes paginated responses without risk. |
| 3 | NIT | `boundKey` (line 164) uses a hardcoded prefix length of 83; while safe for the 124-byte limit, it lacks a constant definition explaining the derivation (124 - 1 separator - 16 hash - 24 buffer). | ACTIONED | Derivation formula (124 byte limit - 1 separator - 16 SHA256 suffix - 24 buffer = 83 prefix) documented in go/gdrivestore/gdrivestore.go. |
| 4 | NIT | `fileToObjectInfo` (line 595) ignores the error from `strconv.ParseInt`; while Drive API usually returns valid integers, the error should be handled to ensure `ObjectInfo.Size` integrity. | ACTIONED | Size parsing in fileToObjectInfo safely defaults to 0 and fallbacks to Content-Length on media get. |

--- SUMMARY (review) ---
  The Google Drive adapter successfully implements the `datastore.ObjectStore` interface using a direct REST approach, satisfying the zero-SDK requirement.
  The "Write-Then-Delete" policy and permanent delete logic meet the acceptance criteria for data integrity and collision handling.
  Top risk remains the in-memory buffering during `Put`, which limits scalability for multi-gigabyte objects despite the "True Streaming" claim in documentation.
